item.title: Case Report: A modified Karapandzic flap with bilateral V-Y advancement for reconstruction of a large full-thickness lower lip defect after squamous cell carcinoma excision
item.description: CONCLUSION: Bilateral V-Y advancement based on the modified Karapandzic concept may provide a reconstructive option for selected extensive full-thickness lower lip defects without formal neurovascular dissection. Although flap survival and oral competence were maintained in this case, postoperative microstomia and the anticipated need for secondary commissuroplasty should be considered during surgical planning.

item.title: Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography detection of a mobile echogenic structure at the left atriotomy suture line - A case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Careful post-bypass TEE examination, including systematic assessment of atriotomy closure sites, may identify potentially embolic mobile echogenic structures and guide surgical management, thereby contributing to perioperative patient safety.

item.title: Behind Closed Doors: Caregiving Burden in Exclusive Two-Person Living Arrangements
item.description: This study examined caregiving burden among primary family caregivers in two-person households, consisting solely of home-based Long-Term Care Insurance recipients and their caregivers in South Korea. By analyzing 1,068 caregivers from the 2019 and 2022 Korean Long-Term Care Surveys (717 spouses; 351 adult children), we assessed burden across emotional support, IADL, housekeeping, and physical ADL domains. Spousal caregivers showed higher odds of IADL and physical ADL burden, and caregiving...

item.title: Social Determinants of Health Associated With Unhealthy Weight Management Behaviors Among Emerging Adult Women: Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: UWMBs are widely practiced among emerging adult women and are associated with both intermediary body image-related factors and broader sociocultural norms when considered simultaneously. These findings underscore the need for interventions that address appearance-related norms, particularly those disseminated through social media environments, rather than approaches focused solely on individual determinants. Future research should clarify the mechanisms linking structural and...

item.title: Hospital-level sepsis bundle compliance and its association with hospital performance in sepsis and septic shock in a nationwide cohort study
item.description: The sepsis bundle was developed to standardize sepsis treatment and improve patient outcomes. Although public health authorities have promoted its use, the impact of hospital-level compliance on patient outcomes, particularly in settings without mandatory sepsis bundle compliance, remains unclear. This prospective cohort study included 11,926 patients aged 19 years or older diagnosed with sepsis or septic shock, admitted to 19 tertiary referral hospitals from September 1, 2019, to December 31,...

item.title: Defining the levels of the chromatin landscape using the I-CATCH system
item.description: Alterations of the epigenome, including histone tail post-translational modifications (PTMs), have been shown to regulate the expression of genes important for driving multiple cellular processes including cellular differentiation, aging and tumorigenesis. Although the ability to measure histone tail PTM levels is integral to the understanding of chromatin biology, because of technological limitations, the proportion of nucleosomes that have histone tail PTMs at genomic loci remain undefined. To...

item.title: Acute Levothyroxine Overdose Followed by Serial Monitoring of Total Thyroxine and Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone in a Hypothyroid Dog
item.description: Reports of acute levothyroxine overdose in dogs are rare with limited monitoring data. An 8-year-old spayed female Pomeranian receiving long-term hypothyroidism treatment presented 9 h after ingesting a one-month supply of levothyroxine (3 mg; 1.13 mg/kg). Except for transient tachycardia, the physical examination revealed unremarkable findings. The total thyroxine (T4) level exceeded the upper limit of quantification. Levothyroxine was discontinued, and activated charcoal and intravenous fluid...

item.title: Expert Strategies: Controversies in Management of Sinonasal Malignancies-Global Perspectives Through a Mixed Methods Approach
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Management of SNMs is complex, with a wide variety of practice patterns among experts. This work serves as a modern guide for expert management paradigms where little data currently exists.

item.title: Machine Learning Guided Meta-transcriptomics Reveals OsRPM1 as a Key Regulator of Rice Blast Resistance
item.description: Rice blast, caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, is the most destructive fungal disease of rice, responsible for annual yield losses of 10-30% and posing a major threat to global food security. The rapid evolution of blast pathotypes and the polygenic nature of resistance complicate breeding efforts for durable resistance. In this study, we integrated multiple RNA-sequencing datasets, revealing a dynamic transcriptional landscape during infection. Compared with susceptible genotypes, resistant...

item.title: The interplay of physical activity and climate change perceptions in shaping perceived heat tolerance among senior people in Poland and Spain
item.description: Although physical activity is widely promoted for healthy ageing, its relationship with perceived heat tolerance-especially under growing climate concern-remains unclear. This study examines how physical activity frequency relates to perceived heat tolerance among older adults and whether this association is conditioned by climate change concern and perceived health risks. The study employed Granular Interaction Thinking Theory and Bayesian Mindsponge Framework analytics to analyze data from...

item.title: Diazonium-mediated interfacial coupling enables efficient charge transport in MXene/Te hybrid papers
item.description: Efforts to develop high-performance, free-standing MXene-based thermoelectric materials have frequently been hindered by insufficient interfacial coupling and the environmental reactivity of MXenes, particularly their susceptibility to oxidation under aqueous conditions. In this study, a free-standing MXene/Te composite paper was fabricated by integrating MXene nanosheets with Te nanowires, followed by diazonium-mediated interfacial modification. Before diazonium treatment, the MXene/Te paper...

item.title: Neurological Outcomes of Rhythm Transitions in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest With Initial Nonshockable Rhythms: A Nationwide Population-Based Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Asystole conversion to PEA during CPR was associated with a better neurologic outcome than persistent asystole. Although transitioning from PEA to asystole was associated with lower odds of a good outcome compared with persistent PEA, it was associated with a better outcome than A-P transitions. Recognizing these patterns may provide prognostic context beyond a single rhythm assessment.

item.title: Age-Adjusted PI-LL Versus L1 Pelvic Angle for Discriminating Proximal Junctional Kyphosis in Lower Thoracic Fusion for Adult Spinal Deformity
item.description: CONCLUSION: The 2 indices discriminated PJK comparably, but only a negative L1PA offset identified patients at increased risk. When the 2 targets conflict, the L1PA target can be used as the more informative boundary.

item.title: Co-Creating Disaster Alert Messages with Communities for Climate Adaptation and Public Health
item.description: This study examines how to improve the effectiveness of climate-related disaster alert messages. Using a living lab methodology-based co-creation approach, it conducts a case study in Seoul, South Korea, exploring how citizens and experts can collaboratively enhance disaster alert messages. Findings showed that citizens perceive current disaster alert messages as lacking relevance, causing desensitization to alerts, and providing insufficient information. Moreover, citizens indicated that...

item.title: Dynamics of within-host genomic relatedness and emergence of resistance in serial Mycobacterium avium complex isolates during treatment
item.description: Mycobacterium avium complex infections require prolonged multidrug therapy and may develop antimicrobial resistance. We applied whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to assess within-patient genomic relatedness and resistance-associated mutations emerging during therapy. WGS was performed on cultured populations of 30 serial isolates (16 M. avium and 14 Mycobacterium intracellulare) from 13 patients with repeated recovery of the same species. Genomic relatedness was classified by species/subspecies,...

item.title: Metabolic and Renal Dysfunction Are Associated With Intraplaque Lipid Burden Assessed by Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Intravascular Ultrasound: Insights Into the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic and renal dysfunction are independently associated with intraplaque lipid burden assessed by near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound. These findings provide intracoronary imaging evidence linking the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework to plaque-level lipid accumulation.

item.title: Longitudinal Inflammatory Trajectories and Recurrent Vascular Events After Acute Ischemic Stroke
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Persistent high IBI trajectories were independently associated with recurrent stroke and MACE, and persistent high hs-CRP trajectories were associated with MACE. Longitudinal assessment of inflammatory biomarkers may provide prognostic information beyond a single baseline measurement after ischemic stroke.

item.title: Comparison of 1-Year Clinical Outcomes Following SmartSight Lenticule Extraction Among Three Different Astigmatism Groups
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The 12-month follow-up data show that SmartSight treatments for correction of myopia and myopic astigmatism with the SCHWIND ATOS is a safe, efficient, and accurate procedure irrespective of the level of preoperative astigmatism. However, a trend for refractive undercorrection was found for increasing astigmatism levels, partly reflected in the visual outcomes.

item.title: Sex-Specific Molecular Patterns Reveal Distinct Age-Associated Arterial Wall Remodeling
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Internal thoracic arteries from elderly patients with coronary artery disease exhibit distinct sex-specific arterial wall remodeling patterns, with immune-suppressed proliferative remodeling in males and stress-associated extracellular matrix vulnerability in females. These findings provide a biological framework for understanding sex differences in age-associated arterial remodeling and may provide context for sex disparities in cardiovascular outcomes.

item.title: Case Report: Delayed epirubicin extravasation-induced ulceration in a dog managed without surgical intervention using adjunctive hyperbaric gaseous cryotherapy
item.description: Extravasation of anthracyclines can result in progressive tissue injury, ulceration, and necrosis, and may ultimately require surgical intervention. Management of delayed presentations remains challenging, as recommended treatments, including dexrazoxane, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and cold compresses, are most effective when initiated promptly after the extravasation event. A 9-year-old spayed female Poodle with suspected stage IV multicentric lymphoma developed a progressive ulcerative lesion...

item.title: Electroreduction of diluted CO<sub>2</sub> to formic acid enabled by protic ionic liquid interfaces
item.description: Using diluted instead of pure CO(2) from combustion waste streams for electrocatalytic CO(2) reduction (ECR) can lower gas purification costs and improve commercial competitiveness, but direct ECR under dilute CO(2) feeds is limited by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and low cathodic current densities. Here, we report a Bi catalyst modified with a protic ionic liquid prepared from a strong base (1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU)) and a weak acid (trifluoroethanol (TFE))...

item.title: Discovery of new polyacetylenes from the rhizomes of Adenia cardiophylla through activity-directed phytochemical investigation and evaluation of their anti-inflammatory properties
item.description: Adenia cardiophylla (Mast.) Engl. Passifloraceae has long been used in traditional medicine throughout Vietnam and Southeast Asia for the treatment of rheumatism, bone pain, and pneumonia. Based on bioassay-guided isolation, seven previously undescribed compounds, including one cyanogenic glycoside (1), four polyacetylenes (2-4, 6), and two cyclopentene carboxylic acid derivatives (20 and 21), together with sixteen known compounds from the rhizomes of Adenia cardiophylla were isolated. The...

item.title: Polydeoxyribonucleotide and polynucleotide effects in musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review
item.description: CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Available evidence suggests potential improvements in pain and function following PDRN/PN treatment; however, the certainty of the evidence remains limited because of methodological limitations, heterogeneous study designs, and inconsistent comparative effects. The limited quality and geographic representativeness of the evidence warrant rigorous, prospectively registered, large-scale, multinational randomized controlled trials.

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Feasibility and acceptability of a mindfulness-based vitality promotion program in a lifelong learning setting: a single-arm mixed-methods study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Mixed-methods findings provide preliminary information regarding the feasibility and acceptability of the MVP program and indicate favorable pre-post changes in several self-reported health-related outcomes. The MVP program may represent a practical lifelong learning intervention with potential relevance for public health promotion. Further controlled studies are warranted to establish its efficacy.

item.title: Subregional neuromelanin-sensitive MRI of the substantia nigra is associated with striatal dopaminergic function in early-stage Parkinson's disease
item.description: Neuromelanin-sensitive magnetic resonance imaging (NM-MRI) enables radiation-free assessment of nigral dopaminergic integrity in Parkinson's disease (PD), but its quantitative relationship with striatal dopaminergic function has not been well established. We therefore investigated whether NM-MRI-derived volumes of the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) are associated with striatal dopamine transporter availability measured by ^(18)F-FP-CIT positron emission tomography (PET) in early-stage PD....

item.title: Reconceptualizing employee engagement: toward a relational, existential alternative
item.description: Employee engagement has become one of the most influential constructs in organizational scholarship, yet its centrality has rarely been matched by conceptual scrutiny. This article examines employee engagement through three converging issues: a largely unexamined presumption that engagement is inherently good, a definitional ambiguity produced by persistent jingle-jangle phenomena and by a growing gap between what engagement measures claim to capture and what they actually measure, and a...

item.title: Redefining drug-induced tremor: a mechanism-based framework for clinical and etiological assessment
item.description: Drug-induced tremor (DIT) encompasses clinically diverse syndromes with different mechanisms, clinical courses, and management needs. This Perspective proposes a mechanism-based approach to guide evaluation and management by integrating tremor phenotype, drug pharmacology, associated neurological findings, and clinical course. The initial assessment considers peripheral adrenergic amplification, dopamine receptor blockade or depletion, and systemic or neurotoxic effects, while allowing...

item.title: Owning what one did not make: psychological ownership, agency, and the authorship legitimation deficit in human-AI co-creation
item.description: Authorship can align three relations to a work: experiencing it as one's own, feeling like the agent behind it, and standing answerable for it. Effortful engagement can support this alignment, an arrangement this article calls the labor nexus of authorship, but direction, selection, editing, and authority over release also matter. Generative artificial intelligence can separate initial-production effort from the resulting product without uniformly weakening ownership, agency, or responsibility....

item.title: Patient-reported outcomes from ASCENT-03: sacituzumab govitecan vs chemotherapy in advanced triple-negative breast cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SG provided meaningful and sustained benefits in QOL vs chemotherapy. Although SG is associated with known increased gastrointestinal side effects, they can be managed and did not adversely affect functioning, long-term QOL, or treatment tolerability. These data complement previous efficacy results and support first-line SG as a new standard of care for patients with mTNBC who are not candidates for PD-(L)1 inhibitors.(ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05382299).

item.title: Artificial Intelligence in Temporomandibular Joint Imaging: Diagnostic Performance Across Input Modality-Target Pairings-A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Sensitivity was higher when disc displacement was depicted directly on magnetic resonance imaging than when inferred from imaging that does not depict the disc. However, the cross-domain group contained only three estimates, the omnibus pairing test was not significant, and design factors were entangled. Performance should therefore be interpreted by pairing, while direct depiction versus proxy inference requires prospective testing.

item.title: Phenotypic diversity in Pierson syndrome: a case report of absent microcoria and mild renal progression
item.description: Infantile nephrotic syndrome (INS) is a heterogeneous kidney disorder characterized by proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and edema within the first year of life. INS has a high prevalence of genetic mutations, resulting in an aggressive clinical course. Pierson syndrome manifests as congenital nephrotic syndrome, microcoria, and neurological abnormalities. However, the phenotypic spectrum is increasingly recognized as variable. We report a case of a 6-month-old female infant with INS presenting with...

item.title: Mild clinical course in siblings with NPHS1-associated familial nephrotic syndrome: two case reports
item.description: NPHS1-associated nephrotic syndrome (NS) has traditionally been considered a severe hereditary podocytopathy that presents in infancy with heavy proteinuria, poor response to immunosuppressive therapy, and early progression to kidney failure. However, accumulating evidence suggests that the clinical course varies by genotype, with some variants associated with partial preservation of nephrin function and a relatively milder phenotype. We report two brothers with NS onset beyond the congenital...

item.title: Target antigens and antigen-specific clinical phenotypes in pediatric membranous nephropathy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence is insufficient to use antigen status alone for prognostic or treatment stratification in pediatric MN. Nevertheless, antigen typing may refine diagnosis and etiologic evaluation by prompting assessment for autoimmunity or relevant exposures. Serial anti-PLA2R measurement may support patient monitoring although tissue and serum findings are not interchangeable.

item.title: Pediatric stone disease: a urologist's perspective
item.description: Pediatric urolithiasis is increasing in prevalence worldwide and differs from adult stone disease because of its strong associations with metabolic abnormalities, genetic disorders, congenital urinary tract anomalies, and a lifelong risk of recurrence. Urologic management extends beyond stone removal to achieve durable stone-free status while preserving the developing urinary tract and minimizing cumulative treatment burden, including radiation exposure, repeated general anesthesia,...

item.title: Clinical practice recommendations for the management of Alport syndrome: a joint statement of the Korean Society of Nephrology and the Korean Society of Pediatric Nephrology
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Accordingly, these guidelines strongly recommend early RAS blockade as the cornerstone of AS, while no recommendations are made for routine use of cyclosporine, MRAs, or SGLT2i. Well-designed clinical trials are needed to expand therapeutic options and improve longterm outcomes in AS.

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Conversations That Clear the Air: Supportive Parent-Adolescent Communication and Smoking in a Dyadic Perspective
item.description: Despite evidence that family communication shapes adolescent health behaviors, few studies have examined the dyadic associations between parents and adolescents. This study investigates supportive parent-adolescent communication and smoking in both generations. Data from a representative sample of 940 parent-adolescent dyads were analyzed using the Actor-Partner Interdependence Model (APIM) with latent constructs. Results revealed significant actor and partner effects for adolescents: both...

item.title: Age-Stratified Association Between Health Literacy and Unmet Medical Needs among Korean Adults
item.description: Identifying the factors associated with unmet medical need (UMN) is critical for designing interventional strategies. This nationwide cross- sectional study investigated the association between health literacy (HL) and UMN among Korean adults in specific age groups. Data from 5,660 adults who participated in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2023), along with available data on HL and UMN, were analysed. HL was assessed using the Health Literacy Index for the Community....

item.title: Cryo-EM structures of an anti-MLC1 Fab in apo and peptide-bound states reveal the basis of antigen recognition
item.description: Monoclonal antibodies are widely used to detect and characterize membrane proteins, yet for most such reagents, the molecular basis of target recognition remains structurally undefined. Here, we report the structural and biochemical characterization of 37E5, a monoclonal antibody that recognizes MLC1, an astrocytic membrane protein implicated in gliovascular homeostasis and megalencephalic leukoencephalopathy with subcortical cysts. 37E5 specifically detects endogenous MLC1 across multiple...

item.title: Peptide-DNA Hybrid Selection for Chemical Functionality Recognition across Diverse Material Interfaces
item.description: Sequence-defined affinity ligands are powerful tools for molecular recognition, yet their selection has largely focused on defined molecular targets rather than shared chemical functionalities. Extending sequence-based recognition to a chemical moiety presents a distinct challenge because the same functionality must be recognized across structurally and chemically diverse molecular and material contexts. Here, we demonstrate that in vitro selection of peptide-DNA hybrids can generate an affinity...

item.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Vascular Sphincters in the Brain
item.description: Brain precapillary sphincters (PSs) are located at the point where the penetrating arteriole meets the first-order capillary. Sphincters link blood flow in the capillaries to arteriolar inflow. The sphincters are encircled by contractile mural cells that can control the length and width of the enclosed vessel segment in both directions. Hemodynamic consequences include the ability of PSs to generate the largest changes in cerebrovascular flow resistance of all brain vessel segments. Using...

item.title: Prognostic Factors in Lenvatinib-Treated Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A Real-World Study with Extended Follow-Up
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Lenvatinib provided durable disease control in patients with RAI-R DTC. Older age at treatment initiation and bone metastasis were independent determinants of survival and may help guide risk stratification and treatment timing in clinical practice.

item.title: TSPYL2 regulated by miR-301a-3p contributes to impaired decidualization in polycystic ovary syndrome
item.description: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most common endocrine disorders associated with female infertility. Increasing evidence suggests that impaired endometrial receptivity, in addition to ovulatory dysfunction, may contribute to infertility in women with PCOS. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying defective decidualization in PCOS remain poorly understood. We observed impaired decidualization in both a prenatally androgenized mouse model and primary endometrial stromal cells...

item.title: Longitudinal dynamics of gut microbiota maturation and its modulators from infancy through childhood
item.description: Early-life gut microbiota development is closely linked to long-term health. We characterize gut microbiota in 695 Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood 2010 (COPSAC(2010)) children using 16S rRNA gene sequencing of 2,689 fecal samples collected from 1 week to 6 years of age. Gut microbiota development is rapid during the first four years and gradually slows over the subsequent two years. A random forest model predicts microbial age from community composition and defines gut...

item.title: Visible-light-driven C(sp<sup>3</sup>)-P bond formation by a halogen-bonding-assisted EDA-SET/HAT system
item.description: A visible-light-driven C(sp³)-P bond formation reaction mediated by a halogen-bonding-assisted electron donor-acceptor (EDA) system has been developed. The reaction proceeds under photocatalyst-free conditions through an EDA-mediated single-electron transfer (EDA-SET)/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) mechanism. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support the proposed halogen-bonding-assisted EDA-SET/HAT pathway.

item.title: Stratified Analysis of IOL Constant Optimization and Refractive Prediction Accuracy According to Ocular Biometric Parameters: Comparison with Overall Optimization
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: For B-UII, overall optimization of the LF appeared more useful than additional stratified optimization. Although the effect of stratified optimization on absolute prediction error was limited, the directional trends in refractive prediction identified across biometric subgroups may assist in choosing between adjacent IOL powers.

item.title: Assessment of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease severity using deep learning-based kidney volumetry in CT
item.description: CONCLUSION: The proposed method enables accurate TKV quantification and MIC classification from noncontrast CT, supporting severity assessment and longitudinal monitoring in ADPKD.

item.title: Postoperative complications worsen long-term survival in lung cancer surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this meta-analysis may help improve risk assessment for poor survival in patients after lung cancer surgery.

item.title: A pediatric central nervous system tumor with BCOR internal tandem duplication confirmed after initially inconclusive targeted molecular testing: a case report
item.description: Central nervous system (CNS) tumors with BCOR internal tandem duplication (ITD) are a distinct pediatric tumor entity characterized by recurrent exon 15 internal tandem duplication of the BCOR gene and a specific DNA methylation profile. We report a rare case of a 13-month-old girl who presented with a hemorrhagic left parietal tumor. item.title: A case of infant-type hemispheric glioma, ALK-altered, with a 23-year long-term follow-up
item.description: At 3 months of age, a tumorous lesion was detected extending from the right temporal lobe to the occipital lobe, and a craniotomy with tumor resection was performed. The pathological diagnosis was glioblastoma (WHO2000). At 1 year and 5 months of age, a second craniotomy with tumor resection was performed for tumor recurrence, and the diagnosis was recurrent glioblastoma (WHO2000). Chemotherapy was administered for 2 years, after which the patient remained tumor-free. At age 23, following a...

item.title: Preoperative computed tomography measurement for predicting difficulty in hand-sewn ileal pouch-anal anastomosis: a refined single-center cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative PED measurement is a simple and highly accurate predictor of difficulty in achieving a tension-free hand-sewn IPAA. A PED of 21 cm or greater allows surgeons to optimize the surgical approach and prepare for advanced mesenteric lengthening maneuvers.

item.title: Perspectives of rheumatologists on the management of late-onset rheumatoid arthritis: a nationwide cross-sectional survey
item.description: With population ageing, the number of patients with late-onset rheumatoid arthritis (LORA) is increasing. However, optimal treatment strategies remain unclear. We aimed this study to clarify the current perspectives of rheumatologists regarding the management of LORA. We conducted an anonymous online questionnaire for members of the Japan College of Rheumatology between March and May 2023. The questionnaire consisted of multiple-choice questions about their perspectives on the concept and...

item.description: The Fontan operation enables long term survival for many individuals born with single ventricle heart disease, but the resulting circulation imposes a lifelong hemodynamic burden and predisposes to cardiovascular dysfunction and multisystem morbidity. Evidence based guidance for assessment and management of Fontan specific cardiac and vascular dysfunction, however, remains limited. The European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN) convened an international, multidisciplinary...

item.title: Hydroxyapatite-based aqueous two-phase capillary suspensions for injectable scaffolds
item.description: Artificial bone materials are a new therapeutic strategy to overcome the shortage of donors and the risk of complications associated with conventional bone grafting. Injectable materials are being investigated for their potential application in bone tissue regeneration as materials that can be delivered to bone defects using a minimally invasive method. Capillary suspensions are three-phase systems comprising solid particles, a dispersing medium, and a secondary immiscible fluid; they exhibit...

item.title: Origin of Divergent H/D Isotope Effects on 31P NMR Chemical Shifts in Ferrocene Derivatives: A Multicomponent DFT Study
item.description: The hydrogen-bonded neutral ferrocene-1,1'-diyl-bis(methylphosphinic acid) (FcPMe) and its monoanion (FcPMe(-)) exhibit divergent H/D isotope effects on their 31P NMR chemical shifts (δP). item.description: The vibronically coupled broad infrared (IR) absorption of self-assembled tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) derivative monolayers on functional alkanethiolate-covered Au(111) surfaces was studied by infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (IRAS), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations. item.title: Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity in Photoinduced Charge-Separations of Cryptochrome: Potential Role in Magnetoreception
item.description: Radical-pair-based magnetic compass mechanisms are believed to depend on spin-selective reaction pathways modulated by the Earth's magnetic field. However, the influence of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) on the magnetic compass function at the molecular level remains largely unknown. item.description: Electrochemical two-electron CO2 reduction (2e- CO2RR) to carbon monoxide (CO) and formic acid (HCOOH) on single-atom catalysts (SACs) has long been rationalized by independent reaction pathways initiated from distinct CO2 adsorption modes. item.title: Unveiling Cation-Polymer Coordination: A Reverse Approach from Neutron Scattering in Dilute Acetonitrile Solutions
item.description: Quantifying cation coordination is essential for understanding ion transport in solid polymer electrolytes, yet reliable experimental determination of coordination numbers remains challenging. Here, we establish a calibrated framework that integrates Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy with neutron total scattering data to quantify cation coordination environments relevant to polymer electrolytes. item.description: Although hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) reactions broadly follow the Bell-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) relationship, the physical origin of systematic deviations from this relationship remains insufficiently understood. Here, we combine high-level DLPNO-CCSD(T) barrier calculations for 400 HAT reactions and their reverse reactions with interpretable machine learning to identify a compact set of physically meaningful descriptors associated with activation barriers beyond reaction thermodynamics. item.title: Anticipated Threat Amplifies Esophageal Perception in the Absence of Peripheral Change
item.description: CONCLUSIONS & INFERENCES: Threat amplified perceived intensity and fear in response to neutral esophageal stimulation. Contrary to expectations, response times were slower under threat, suggesting threat may potentially interfere with rather than facilitate behavioral responding. These findings support a role for threat-related processes in esophageal symptom perception.

item.title: From Sensitivity to Temporal Fidelity in Wearable Sweat Sensing
item.description: Wearable sweat sensors are judged mainly by analytical sensitivity, yet a detection limit cannot tell when a measured concentration was secreted. At low or intermittent sweat rates, fluid retained in the device delays and mixes successive samples, so each reading reflects a distribution of sample ages rather than a single moment. item.description: Antimony (Sb) and bismuth (Bi) are promising alloy-type anode materials for potassium-ion batteries (PIBs), yet Sb suffers from a massive 390% volume expansion during potassiation, while Bi is limited by a relatively low specific capacity of 384 mAh·g-1. Moreover, existing synthesis methods for BiSb alloys are complex, costly, and require binders or conductive additives that impair electrochemical performance. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: RW-ISR restored calibration without compromising discrimination. Notably, clinical Cox achieved discrimination comparable to RSF (median C-index 0.770 for both) and superior calibration, indicating that the more complex machine-learning model did not confer additional predictive benefit over standard regression in this older population. Here we investigate the role of water for the thermal decomposition of the noble-gas hydride HXeCl in the HXeCl-H/D(2)O complex. The study was carried out via ab initio calculations and Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics (AIMD) simulations. item.title: C/EBP-β-mediated upregulation of CaV1.2 calcium channel increases arterial constriction in mice with ibrutinib-associated hypertension
item.description: Ibrutinib, a Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor, is indicated for treating chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), but hypertension is a common cardiovascular adverse event. Previous studies have linked ibrutinib to cardiac events through dysregulated intracellular calcium handling, but the mechanisms underlying ibrutinib-associated hypertension remain largely unknown. item.title: Phase 2a study of readthrough therapy in nonsense mutation Alport syndrome
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings provide first-in-human evidence of exaluren-mediated collagen IV readthrough and justify further trials in Alport syndrome and other nonsense mutation-driven kidney diseases, which often cause early-onset kidney failure.

item.title: Transcriptional regulation of NK cell state by ELF4 links innate immune licensing to kidney fibrosis
item.description: Fibrosis is a common outcome of chronic tissue injury, yet immune regulators that are conserved across species and translatable to human disease remain poorly defined. By integrating human kidney transcriptomes with multiple murine models of kidney fibrosis, we identified the ETS transcription factor ELF4 as a conserved, immune-enriched regulator associated with disease severity. item.title: Perioperative Camrelizumab Plus Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this phase 2 randomized clinical trial, perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved EFS with manageable toxic effects, supporting evaluation of intensified perioperative immune priming in resectable HNSCC.

item.title: Izalontamab Brengitecan in Recurrent or Metastatic Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: The PANKU-Esophagus01 Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Izalontamab brengitecan significantly improved PFS and OS vs chemotherapy in patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC whose disease had progressed after first-line treatment. These findings support izalontamab brengitecan as a new second-line treatment for this population in China.

item.description: Across two studies, we examined whether endorsement of color-blind racial attitudes (color-blindness) impact perceptions of patient fit for clinical trials. item.title: Pathogen-specific salvage of totally implantable ports and the role of antibiotic lock therapy
item.description: CONCLUSION: TIP salvage was associated with the infecting organism. The pathogen gradient mirrored guideline-based removal recommendations. About 60% of attempted retentions succeeded, without detectable benefit of ALT. With a pathogen-stratified protocol, salvage can be attempted in selected patients.

item.title: Efficacy, Acceptability, and Tolerability of Trazodone in Insomnia Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Trazodone was associated with short-term improvement in subjective sleep quality among heterogeneous populations with insomnia symptoms. The most observable benefit appears to occur at relatively low doses, while dose escalation may offer limited additional benefit and reduce tolerability. However, interpretation of the findings is limited by considerable clinical heterogeneity, sparse evidence at higher doses, and insufficient data on long-term efficacy and safety.

item.title: Treatment Engagement and Facial Emotion Recognition among Adolescent Males and Females with Conduct Problems
item.description: Few studies have empirically tested whether facial emotion recognition (FER) is related to treatment engagement (TE), which is unfortunate since TE is crucial for treatment success. This study investigated whether FER abilities were associated with TE among adolescent males and females who have (allegedly) committed crimes and/or exhibited conduct problems. item.title: Humanistic Burden of Sjögren's Disease: A Systematic Review of Treatment Efficacy on Health-Related Quality of Life
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Systemic treatments have generally focused on disease activity parameters and have shown limited efficacy in reducing patient-reported symptoms as measured using HRQoL tools in SjD, leaving a significant unmet need for patient-centered holistic therapies.

item.title: Prescription Coverage Following Initiation of HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) in a National Cohort of United States Veterans
item.description: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is 99% effective in preventing HIV infection when used as prescribed, but barriers to initiation and coverage limit its impact. U.S. military Veterans should have improved access to PrEP through the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). However, limited data suggests that most Veterans who are vulnerable to HIV are not prescribed PrEP, and many do not continue PrEP even when clinically indicated. item.title: Impact of lung cancer screening on the workload of radiology professionals
item.description: CONCLUSION: Although LCS increased workload for many radiology professionals, few reported feeling overworked. Despite the added demands, there may be added benefits for radiology professionals. Taken together, these findings emphasise the importance of continuously evaluating and monitoring how LCS affects the workload of radiology healthcare professionals.
